in_sanskrit.name: राजनारायण
in_sanskrit.meaning: राज (Raj) - king, राय (Raya) - advisor, नारायण (Narayan) - God Vishnu
in_sanskrit.long_meaning: The one who rules and advises (Raja) the God Vishnu (Narayan)

in_hindi.name: राजनारायण
in_hindi.meaning: राज (Raj) - राजा (Raja) - king, नारायण (Narayan) - नरायण (Narayan) - God Vishnu
in_hindi.long_meaning: The one who rules (Raja) as a king (Raj) the God Vishnu (Narayan)

in_tamil.name: ராஜ்நாராயண

in_tamil.long_meaning: The one who rules (Raj) as a king (Raj) the God Vishnu (Narayanam)

in_telugu.long_meaning: The one who rules (Raj) as a king (Raj) the God (Narayan) Eshwar

data.cultural_impact: The name Rajnarayan holds great cultural significance in Hinduism, representing the idea of a divine monarch who rules over the universe. This name has been used for several deities and also for royal figures.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name Rajnarayan signifies the presence of God (Narayan) within an individual, making them a king (Raj) in the spiritual realm. The understanding is that each soul is a microcosm of the universe and contains the divine.

name_in_real_life.story: A devoted individual named Lakshmi Rajnarayan in Bali, Indonesia attributes much of their spiritual journey to their name Rajnarayan, which means "King of Kings, Lord of Gods". They believe their name has guided them on the path of righteousness.

data.spiritual_symbolism: Rajnarayan: King of Gods (Raja - king, Narayan - God). Symbolizes the pursuit of divine kingship in one's life, embodying both worldly power and spiritual enlightenment.

The name Rajnarayan is a combination of two Sanskrit words, Raj (King) and Narayan (God).
